# Part 2

## Question 1: Use read_csv (from readr library) to read the tweets CSV file. Name the dataset as tweets_data
```{r}
tweets_data <- read_csv("HW1 - Input_Tweets.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Question 2: Create a new column in the tweets_data as tweet length using mutate function of “dplyr” library. Capture the average tweets length to answer the first question, “What is the typical word length for a social customer service response?” Use an appropriate function from the stringr library. The question can be answered using ncar()

```{r}
tweets_data <- tweets_data %>% 
  mutate(tweets_length=str_count(text))

mean(tweets_data$tweets_length)
```
The mean tweets length is 92.14379

## Question 3: How many tweets in the dataset are less than 50 characters in length? Remove the tweets from the dataset that are less than 50 characters.

```{r}
tweets_data %>%
  filter(tweets_length < 50) %>% 
  nrow()

filter_tweets_data<-tweets_data %>%
  filter(tweets_length >= 50)

filter_tweets_data
```
## Question 4: Convert all the tweets to lowercase using the appropriate function from “stringr”.  Use tweets_data dataset. 

```{r}
tweets_data<-tweets_data %>%
  mutate(text = str_to_lower(text))
head(tweets_data)
```

## Question 5: Find how many tweets have the word, “pls”. Use str_detect function from the “stringr” library. 
```{r}
tweets_data %>%
  mutate(text = str_to_lower(text)) %>%
  filter(str_detect(text, "pls")) %>%
  nrow()
```
The number of tweet contain "pls" is: 152

## Question 6: Replace “pls” with “please” using “sub” function. Assign the new text to updated_tweet column.  Sub function is part of base implementation. Search for ?sub() 
```{r}
tweets_data<-tweets_data %>%
  mutate(text = str_to_lower(text)) %>%
  mutate(updated_tweet = sub("pls","please",text))
head(tweets_data)
```

## Question 7: Use mgsub of qdap library to replace “pls” and “thanks” with “please” and “thank you” respectively in a single statement.

#### Before transformation:
```{r}
declacration<-tweets_data %>%
  mutate(text = str_to_lower(text)) %>%
  filter(str_detect(text, "pls")&str_detect(text, "thanks")) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  select(text)

declacration$text
```

#### After transformation
```{r}
mgsub(c("pls","thanks"), c("please", "thank you"), declacration)
```

## Question 8: Using the month, date, and year, columns, create a new column response_date column. Make sure that the response_date is of date type.
```{r}
month_patterns <-c('Jan','Feb', 'Mar','Apr', 'May','Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep','Oct', 'Nov','Dec')
month_replacements <-seq(1:12)

day_patterns <- c("Mon","Tue","Wed","Thu","Fri","Sat","Sun")
day_replacements <- seq(1:7)

tweets_data$month_numeric <- mgsub(month_patterns,month_replacements,tweets_data$month)
tweets_data$day_numeric <- mgsub(day_patterns,day_replacements,tweets_data$weekday)

tweets_data["response_date"] <- mdy(str_c(tweets_data$month,"/",tweets_data$date,"/",tweets_data$year))
tweets_data$response_date <- as.Date(tweets_data$response_date)

tweets_data
```

## Question 9: Each tweet has agent initials towards the end of the tweet. E.g., @BigGucciQueen  What country are you calling from? *DD, DD is the agent who responded to customer, BigGucciQueen. Extract the agent initials to a new column agent. To do this assignment, use the appropriate stringr substring function. 
```{r}
pattern="[*][a-z]+"
tweets_data<-tweets_data %>%
  mutate(agent=str_extract(text,pattern))%>%
  replace_na(list(agent=" "))

head(tweets_data)
```

## Question 2: Which links were mentioned the most?
The most mentioned links are:
```{r}
url_pattern <- "http[s]?://(?:[a-zA-Z]|[0-9]|[$-_@.&+]|[!*\\(\\),]|(?:%[0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]))+"

tweets_data %>%
  filter(str_detect(text, url_pattern))%>%
  mutate(link=str_extract(text, url_pattern))%>%
  count(link,sort = TRUE)%>%
  slice(1:4)
```

```{r}
tweets_data %>%
  filter(!agent==" ")%>%

  slice(1:5)
```
The agent is the most hard-working is the one with the initials PL (104 responses).

```{r}
tweets_data %>%
  filter(!agent==" ")%>%
  count(agent) %>%
  nrow()
```
The number of agents available or currently team size is 33.

```{r}
tweets_data %>%
  filter(!agent==" ")%>%
  nrow()
```
The number of tweets with reply is 1180.

```{r}
tweets_data %>%
  filter(agent==" ")%>%
  nrow()
```
The number of unanswered tweets is 197.

We could therefore assume that the number of agents needed to respond to all the tweets is the ideal team size.

```{r}
size=33*192/1180 +33
size
```
The team size should be: 39

# Part 3 (IMDB dataset)

## Question 1: Load data
```{r}
imdb_dataset <- read_csv("IMDB Dataset.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Question 2: Pre-processing
```{r}
imdb_dataset <- imdb_dataset %>%
    mutate(review = str_replace_all(review, "<br />", " ")) %>%
    mutate(review = str_remove_all(review, "[!@#%^*-?'&,+]")) %>%
    mutate(review = str_remove_all(review, '\"')) %>%
    mutate(review = str_replace_all(review, '\\.', " ")) %>%
    mutate(review = str_remove_all(review, "[:punct:]")) %>%
    mutate(review = str_squish(review)) %>%
    mutate(review = str_to_lower(review))
```

### Delete stop worp
```{r}
df<-imdb_dataset %>% 
  mutate(sno = row_number()) %>%
  unnest_tokens(word, review) %>%
  anti_join(stop_words) %>%
  group_by(sno) %>%
  mutate(review = str_c(word, collapse = " ")) %>%
  distinct(review)

imdb_dataset$review <- df$review
```

## Question 3

### Get lexicons
```{r}
afinn<-get_sentiments("afinn")
nrc<-get_sentiments("nrc")
```

```{r}
afinn_pred<-imdb_dataset %>% 
  mutate(sno = row_number()) %>%
  unnest_tokens(word, review) %>%
  left_join(afinn, by="word") %>%
  group_by(sno) %>%
  summarise(score=sum(value,na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(pred_sentiment=case_when(
    score > 0 ~ "positive",
    score < 0 ~ "negative"
  ))%>%
  select(sno,pred_sentiment)

afinn_pred
```


## Question 4
```{r}
nrc<-nrc %>%
  mutate(
    value=case_when(
      sentiment=="negative" ~ -1,
      sentiment=="positive" ~ 1
    )
  )
  

nrc_pred<-imdb_dataset %>% 
  mutate(sno = row_number()) %>%
  unnest_tokens(word, review) %>%
  select(sno,word) %>%
  left_join(filter(nrc, sentiment %in% c("negative","positive")), by="word")%>%
  replace_na(list(value=0)) %>%
  group_by(sno) %>%
  summarise(score=sum(value,na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(pred_sentiment=case_when(
    score > 0 ~ "positive",
    score <= 0 ~ "negative"
  ))%>%
  select(sno,pred_sentiment)
  
nrc_pred
```



## Question 5

### Afinn lexicons
```{r}
confusionMatrix1 <- as.data.frame(table(as.factor(imdb_dataset$sentiment), as.factor(afinn_pred$pred_sentiment)))

colnames(confusionMatrix1)<-c("true_value","predicted_value","Frequency")

plotCM <- confusionMatrix1 %>% 
  inner_join( (confusionMatrix1 %>% 
                       group_by(true_value) %>%
                       summarize(total = sum(Frequency))), # Getting the ratio of success/failure
              by = "true_value") %>%
  mutate(ratio = Frequency/total, 
         success_failure = ifelse(true_value == predicted_value, 
                                  "success", "failure")) %>%
  select(true_value, predicted_value, success_failure, ratio)

# Plot the confusion matrix
ggplot(plotCM, 
       mapping = aes(x = true_value, y = predicted_value, 
                     fill = success_failure, 
                     alpha = ratio)) + 
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(ratio,2), "%"), vjust = 1, fontface  = "bold", alpha = 1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(success = "green", failure = "red")) +
  labs(title="Confusion Matrix - Frequency and ratio",
       subtitle="of Afinn lexicon prediction") +
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

confusionMatrix(as.factor(imdb_dataset$sentiment), as.factor(afinn_pred$pred_sentiment))
```
The accuracy is: 0.7342

```
